subject: Middlesex Avenue Safety Advocacy
overview: The commission planned a formal response to a fatal crash on Middlesex Avenue and discussed strategies to secure funding and installation for city-wide bike racks. The body also recapped recent community cycling events and addressed the resignation of a long-term member.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved minutes for the June, July, August, and September meetings.

items.title: Member Resignation and Recruitment
items.summary: Accepted the resignation of Pat Bivins and approved opening a formal call for new membership applications to fill upcoming vacancies.

items.title: Middlesex Avenue Fatal Crash Response
items.summary: Approved sending a letter to MassDOT requesting a formal safety review and infrastructure improvements following a fatal pedestrian crash on the state-owned portion of Middlesex Avenue.

items.title: Event Recaps
items.summary: Recapped the success of Bike and Walk to School Day and the Harvest Your Energy Festival, noting a high demand for bike racks at local schools.

items.title: Blue Bikes and Infrastructure Map
items.summary: Reviewed the rollout of new Blue Bike stations and discussed methods for accessing usage data and managing abandoned bikes.

items.title: Bike Rack Funding and Installation
items.summary: Approved drafting a letter to the Mayor and City Council requesting funding for bike racks and suggesting the use of volunteer labor to overcome Department of Public Works staffing shortages.

items.title: Safety Prioritization and Signage
items.summary: Discussed the implementation of Vision Zero and the urgent need for better signage at unmarked four-way intersections following a recent serious collision.

items.title: Youth Cycling Program
items.summary: Discussed potential collaboration with a scholastic mountain bike racing program for Medford students.

items.title: Bike Light Distribution Update
items.summary: Noted the expected arrival of a bike light shipment for a distribution event at local schools planned for November.
